title: Piecewise continuous sampling for minimizing bias in animal behavior metrics
author: Lynch, Colin M.
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-zero

steps.title: Collect continuous behavioral data
steps.instruction: Record a continuous behavioral dataset of harvester ant workers, capturing all occurrences of behavior over the entire observation period.

steps.title: Estimate required sampling time
steps.instruction: Analyze the continuous dataset to estimate the amount of sampling time needed to accurately reconstruct the proportion of time animals spend in each behavioral state; determine the sample size at which the variance of the sample converges on the population variation.

steps.title: Create piecewise continuous intervals
steps.instruction: Divide the estimated total sampling time into equal‑duration intervals and distribute these intervals randomly across the full continuous dataset, implementing the piecewise continuous sampling approach.

steps.title: Calculate sampling errors
steps.instruction: From the randomly placed intervals, compute both time‑dependent error (error that varies with interval position) and time‑independent error (overall sampling error) for the reconstructed behavioral proportions.

steps.title: Determine optimal interval count
steps.instruction: Identify the range of interval counts that simultaneously minimize time‑dependent and time‑independent error; the analysis shows that using 4 to 16 sampling intervals provides the optimal balance.

steps.title: Validate robustness
steps.instruction: Confirm that the optimal 4‑to‑16 interval result holds across different underlying behavioral patterns and is supported by simulation studies, indicating broad applicability of the method.
